I recently dined at this restaurant as part of my weekly mom and daughter date and unfortunately, my experience fell short of expectations. Overall, I would describe the food as average—neither terrible nor impressive.

What was far more disappointing was the depressing level of customer service. From the moment we arrived the waitress took forever to come to the table and lack a welcoming attitude. Service was extremely slow, and it often felt difficult to get the attention of our server when we needed assistance, which we had to rely on other servers from other tables passing by to get a basic order. Request took longer than expected, and there was little effort made to check on our table or ensure we were satisfied with our meal except for one gentleman wearing a blue shirt who noticed we were struggling with the service.

Hospitality is a major part of the restaurant experience and as a Hospitality Manager myself I can see that unfortunately, that aspect was noticeably lacking. A friendly attitude, attentiveness, and professionalism can often make up for average food, but in this case, the poor service overshadowed the entire visit, it must be because they automatically charged 20% gratuity and know money is coming in regardless.

The restaurant has potential since the placw itself is beautiful but significant improvements in customer service are needed. While the food was passable, the overall experience did not justify the price or leave a positive impression. Based on this visit, I would be hesitant to return or recommend it to others.

If you’re looking for one of the best seafood spots in the Bronx, Shaking Crab is a must-visit. This place delivers a full seafood boil experience with bold flavors, a fun atmosphere, and hands-on dining that makes it stand out.

We started with the fried pickles, and they were the perfect appetizer crispy on the outside, tangy inside, and served hot with a sauce that balanced everything out. A great way to kick things off before diving into the main event.

For the main, we went all in on the boil crab, and this is where Shaking Crab really shines. The crab was fresh, juicy, and coated in a rich, buttery sauce packed with garlic and spices. Every bite was messy in the best way, full of flavor, and exactly what you want from a proper seafood boil. The seasoning was bold without being overwhelming, letting the natural sweetness of the crab come through.

The ambiance is lively and casual, perfect for going with friends or family. It has that classic seafood boil vibe tables ready for cracking shells, a fun and energetic crowd, and a setting that encourages you to relax and enjoy the experience. The service was friendly and attentive, making sure everything came out on time and that we had everything we needed throughout the meal.

Overall, if you’re searching for the best seafood boil in the Bronx, Shaking Crab is definitely a spot you need to add to your list. Great food, great energy, and a memorable dining experience from start to finish.

I came here for a team get-together that also lined up with my birthday month, so it was the perfect chance to celebrate — and I’m really glad we did. The vibes were amazing from start to finish: great music (major shoutout to the DJ), perfect lighting, and a lively, fun atmosphere that made the night feel special.

The food was fantastic and the portions were huge — seriously, two or three people could’ve eaten from my plate alone. I ordered the pernil with rice and beans, plus a variety appetizer platter. The pork was juicy (though I do wish the skin was a little crispier), the beans were flavorful, and both the garlic and chimichurri sauces were top-notch. The potato salad was okay, but overall, the meal delivered big flavor and big portions.

Since it was my birthday, the team surprised me with a birthday flan and tres leches dessert plate that the restaurant provided. It was the perfect ending — sweet, creamy, and delicious. The birthday celebration itself was incredible; you truly feel like a superstar. Between the LED signs, the DJ shoutouts, and your name flashing across the booth screen, the energy was unmatched.

The drinks were just okay, nothing to write home about, but they got the job done. The only other downsides were the limited parking (especially at night) and the two-hour time limit for our party of ten.

Last night we had dinner at Dominick’s in the Bronx, and honestly, it became one of the highlights of our entire New York trip.

From the moment we walked in, the owner treated us like family. Not like customers. Family. The kind of place where you immediately feel welcomed, comfortable, and at home.

The food was absolutely spectacular the kind of Italian food that reminds you why New York is legendary. Every dish felt homemade, full of tradition, love, and pride. You could taste the history in every bite.

What made the experience so special wasn’t just the incredible food… it was the feeling. Sitting there felt less like eating at a restaurant and more like being invited into someone’s home for Sunday dinner.

In a city full of places to eat, Dominick’s gave us something unforgettable: authenticity, warmth, and a memory we’ll talk about for years. I wish I had photos to share but we enjoyed this so much we forgot about our phones.

Special Thank you to Charlie, from this Texas family for such a wonderful night. My family will absolutely be back next time we visit New York!

text.text:
Mario’s of Arthur Avenue—Where Time Stands Still and Service Means Something

This place is old school in all the good ways. The waiter was exceptionally well-trained and provided a level of service that’s become virtually extinct in this city. It feels like peering through a window into an era when they had your table waiting and your favorite dish already on the way.

They started us with a selection of olive oils and pickled carrots that were aggressively spicy in the best possible way—sharp, tangy, and unapologetic.

I ordered the prosciutto and burrata to start, and it was delicious: paper-thin prosciutto, creamy burrata, simple and flawless.

For the main, I took the server’s recommendation and went with the lasagna. Layers of perfectly cooked pasta, rich with flavor, nothing overwrought or trying too hard.

The entire meal felt like being genuinely taken care of…an art form in itself.

Mario’s isn’t chasing trends or trying to reinvent Italian food. It’s just doing what it’s always done, exceptionally well, with the kind of hospitality that makes you feel like a regular even on your first visit.

If you’re taking a trip to Arthur Ave in the Bronx, this is mandatory.

I ordered the 2-for-1 promotion for the pork and cheese pupusas because I was craving them. This was my first time ordering pupusas from this restaurant, so I was looking forward to trying them.

The pupusas arrived hot and seemed freshly made, but despite being hot, they were actually quite hard and not soft at all. The filling was very disappointing—the cheese was barely noticeable, and the pupusas themselves had very little flavor.

They also came without the tomato sauce that normally accompanies pupusas. The sauce I received was extremely spicy, even though the tomato sauce that normally comes with pupusas should not be spicy. The salad was also extremely spicy.

I have had pupusas from other places before, and I consider them a true delight of Salvadoran cuisine. That is why I was really looking forward to enjoying them. Unfortunately, these particular pupusas did not have the texture, filling, or flavor that they should have had. They were hot, but they were hard, the cheese was barely noticeable, and the overall preparation did not meet the expectations I would have for this dish. I would not order these pupusas again.

This is simply my personal experience with this particular order. I am not trying to offend anyone or claim that the restaurant’s other food is not good. Perhaps other dishes are delicious, but unfortunately, this particular order did not meet the standard I expected.

We truly had the best authentic Italian dinner at this amazing restaurant. From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere was warm, welcoming, and friendly. This family-owned restaurant clearly knows Italian cuisine and takes great pride in every dish they serve.

To finish the evening, we were presented with a dessert tray featuring cannoli, panna cotta, ice cream, chocolate lava cake, and tiramisu. Each dessert was absolutely delicious and the perfect ending to a fantastic dining experience.
I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting the area. The combination of outstanding food, attentive service, and welcoming atmosphere makes it a place you'll want to return to again and again.

text.text:
Nestled on Middletown Road in the Bronx, **Da Franco & Tony Ristora** is a testament to the enduring power of a well-executed meal. It is a place where the atmosphere feels like an extension of the neighborhood's heart, but the kitchen operates with a level of sophistication that rivals the city’s most lauded white-tablecloth establishments.

The Prelude: Perfection in a Bite
Our evening began with an order of **Crab Cakes**, and they set a high bar for what was to follow. These were not the breadcrumb-heavy iterations so common elsewhere; instead, they were packed with sweet, flaky crab meat, seared until golden. The texture was impeccable—offering a gentle crunch before melting into a savory, well-seasoned center.

The Main Event:
The entrées showcased a kitchen that understands both the nuance of the robust demands of meat. My wife’s selection, a **Skirt Steak and Lamb Shank combo**, was a carnivore’s dream. The skirt steak was expertly grilled, boasting a deep char while remaining incredibly tender. The lamb shank was the highlight of the plate—braised until the meat practically fell away from the bone in succulent ribbons. Paired with buttery mashed potatoes and crisp, vibrant vegetables, it was a masterclass in balanced, hearty dining.

For my own course, I turned to the **Gamberi Alla Scampi Con Risotto**. It was, quite simply, a revelation. The shrimp were plump and snapped with freshness, swimming in a classic scampi sauce that balanced garlic, lemon, and high-quality butter without overstaying its welcome. The true technical triumph, however, was the risotto. Creamy, rich, and cooked to a perfect *al dente*, it absorbed the brightness of the sauce, creating a dish that felt both indulgent and refined.

The Finale
To conclude, we shared the **Crème Brûlée**. The hallmark of a great custard is the "crack," and this delivered. The caramelized sugar topping shattered perfectly to reveal a cool, velvety interior that was neither too sweet nor too heavy. It was a sophisticated finish to a meal that felt like a celebration.

The Verdict
Da Franco & Tony Ristora isn't just a restaurant; it’s a destination for those who appreciate technical skill paired with genuine warmth. From the precision of the *Gamberi* to the soul-warming depth of the lamb, this is a kitchen that knows exactly what it’s doing. If you are looking for a meal that feels special from the first bite to the last, Middletown Road is calling.
